chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Habib al-Kha'thami, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said: 'I intend to marry a woman, but my parents intended for me to marry another.' He said: 'Marry the one you desire, and leave the one your parents desire.'
ai.seo_question: Does a parent have the right to force a marriage on their child against their will in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of Chapter 32 of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, which discusses the rights of the bride and the hierarchy of marriage guardians (awliya), this hadith clarifies that while parental approval is customary, the individual's personal inclination (hawa) holds decisive weight for the marriage's validity. This ruling supports the Shia juristic view that a mature individual's consent supersedes parental preference, distinguishing between the permissibility of the contract and the social recommendation of parental involvement. It underscores the autonomy of the bride or groom in selecting a spouse, a key principle in Shia family law.
